# Isoxazolone morph videos — horizontal series format

**Scenes:** [`isoxazole_morph_scene.py`](isoxazole_morph_scene.py) — `IsoxazoleFTIR`,
`IsoxazoleC13`, `IsoxazoleUV`, `IsoxazolePL`.
**Data:** [`isoxazole_video_data.py`](isoxazole_video_data.py), auto-generated by
`Academia\isoxazole\gen_video_data.py`.
**Render:** `.\render_isoxazole.ps1 -Method all -Quality h` →
`Chemistry\Methods_Manim\Isoxazole\`.

A **series** variant of [`HORIZONTAL_FORMAT.md`](HORIZONTAL_FORMAT.md): instead of one
molecule with a stepping playhead, an entire congeneric series morphs through one shared
frame — 18 compounds (isoxazole → 3-methylisoxazol-5(4H)-one → 16 arylidene derivatives),
3 s per compound, 0.5 s per transition. ~64 s.

## One deliberate break from HORIZONTAL_FORMAT

Structures are **flat 2D skeletal**, as that format specifies. The only deviation is that
they are not static: each carries the **drugscope wag** — the bounded billboard rock from
`Oscilloscope\osc\drugscope.py::_proj`:

```
theta = ROCK_DEG * sin(2*pi*t / ROCK_PERIOD)     # 32 deg, 13 s
x' = x * cos(theta)     y' = y                   # squash x, leave y, labels upright
```

Bounded is the point: worst-case squash is cos(32°) ≈ 0.85, so the structure never
approaches edge-on and every bond stays readable.

> **A 3D version was built first and replaced.** Free-rotating 3D conformers needed a
> tilted spin axis, a global plane fit and a per-bond depth cue *purely* to stop a
> near-planar molecule collapsing to a line twice per revolution — and still read as a
> tangle at some angles. None of that machinery exists any more. If you are tempted back
> toward 3D for a planar series, that is the cost.

Everything else is inherited: split screen with a divider at `DIVX`, section titles
top-left, trace outline with no fill and no y-axis, BG halos behind functional-group
symbols, and one fixed screen transform (no drift, no per-compound rescale).

## The morph — the part that matters

Compounds are **not cut between**. `gen_video_data.py` walks the series pairwise with an
RDKit MCS and gives each atom a **canonical key it keeps for as long as it matches**, then
lays each structure out with `GenerateDepictionMatching2DStructure` so its shared core
keeps EXACTLY the previous compound's coordinates and the rest is built around it. Scale
and centring are applied ONCE for the whole series — per-molecule normalisation would undo
the constraint. At a transition:

- shared skeleton → left alone at full opacity (identical coordinates, so it is visually
  static through the cut)
- departing substituent → fades out over `XFADE`
- arriving substituent → fades in over the same `XFADE`

The isoxazolone core is continuous for most of the video; the aryl ring changes around it.
Typical persistence is 14–18 of ~17 atoms. It legitimately drops (ISX 8, ISO 9) where the
chemistry really does change — cinnamylidene moves the ring three bonds further out, and
indole is a different ring system entirely.

## Four gotchas that cost real time here

1. **Constrain the depiction, don't just align it.** An independent `Compute2DCoords` per
   molecule places the same ring somewhere else every time, so the supposedly-unchanged
   core jumps at every transition. `GenerateDepictionMatching2DStructure(mol, ref,
   refPatt=<MCS>)` forces it to stay put.
2. **Draw ALL halos before ANY glyph.** Interleaving them (halo, text, halo, text) lets a
   later symbol's halo punch out an earlier symbol's glyph wherever two labels sit close —
   the -OMe methyl next to its own O rendered as "I3" with the CH clipped away.
3. **Cache the symbol glyphs.** `build_mol()` runs ~1900 times; constructing a manim `Text`
   is a full Pango layout + SVG parse. Building each symbol once and copying it made the
   scene **~5× faster** (5-compound `-q l`: >160 s → 32 s). This is the single biggest
   lever in the file.
4. **Keep the spectrum out of `always_redraw`.** It holds still for 3 s; rebuilding a
   500-point trace every frame is pure waste. It is a static mobject that cross-fades.

Smaller ones: depth-cue the bonds (opacity/width by z, drawn back-to-front) or a rotating
3D structure reads as a tangle; clamp both header lines and the method title or long IUPAC
names cross the divider; stagger peak-label leader heights or adjacent bands overprint.

## GPU — measured, not assumed (RTX 2060)

Ethan's standing policy is GPU-by-default, and the Oscilloscope/CuPy+NVENC pattern earns
it. **manim is the exception, and the numbers say so:**

| path | result |
|---|---|
| `--renderer=opengl` | **slower** — 28.9 s vs cairo's 19.0 s on a matched heavy `always_redraw` benchmark |
| NVENC vs libx264 | **no faster** — 2.2 s vs 2.2 s for 180 frames, and ~3.6× larger files |

The bottleneck is Python-side mobject construction, not rasterisation or encode, so the
GPU has nothing to bite on; OpenGL adds per-frame upload cost for geometry rebuilt every
frame. OpenGL also breaks any hand-built `VMobject` — under that renderer manim swaps
`Line`/`Circle`/`Text` for `OpenGL*` variants but a raw `VMobject` stays cairo and cannot
join the resulting `VGroup`. `_VMobj()` in the scene picks the right class; note
`RendererType` is a plain Enum, so `config.renderer == "opengl"` is **always False** and
silently leaves the cairo class. `pat_raman_scene.py` has the same raw-`VMobject` pattern
and would need the same treatment.

**The real wall-clock win is `-Parallel`** — the three methods are independent renders, one
per method, each with its own `--media_dir` (sharing one corrupts `partial_movie_files`).
`-Nvenc` is wired up because it was asked for, but it is not the default.

## Knobs

`HOLD` 3.0 · `XFADE` 0.5 · `INTRO` 1.0 · `SPIN_RATE` 52 °/s · `TILT_DEG` 28 ·
`TARGET_W` 6.2 · `METHOD_HUE` (FTIR amber, ¹³C teal). **UV and PL are themed per compound**: UV by λmax
through the UVRamanStrip colour rule, so the trace travels violet → blue as the donor
strengthens; PL by λ_em through `visible_color` directly — an emission band is the colour
you actually *see* coming off the sample, so ISS renders green (516 nm) and ISG deep red
(~648 nm). The PL scene also carries a per-compound tag ("ICT emission" / "ESIPT ·
keto-tautomer emission" / "non-emissive reference") that cross-fades with the spectrum.

**`ISO_N=4`** renders only the first N compounds — use it for every `-q l` iteration.

## Adding a method

`gen_video_data.py`'s `METHODS` dict drives everything: add a window/label entry and a
branch in `curve()`, re-run it, then add a `TICKS` entry and a `_IsoxazoleMorph` subclass.
Curves are sampled from the same Academia calls that build the PDF sheets, so the videos
cannot drift from `Academia\isoxazole\figures\`.
